slides.title: HIPPA-cratic · Cohort Studio
slides.notes: Pinned 9f0ad46f32a1a76af25baf1aa621ab862f991c45; source and limited isolated synthetic tests. No official score or hosted verification.

slides.title: 1 · Unknown checksum status becomes ok
slides.fix: Use distinct present-but-unverified, hash-verified, changed and missing states.
slides.notes: With an invented sample manifest and no sources.csv, check_data returned ok. The source also takes this branch when an existing file has no frozen checksum entry. The app maps ok to a green check. This conflates readable/present with compared against a known expected checksum. It is not evidence that a file actually changed or that all sidebar statuses claim clinical correctness. Acceptance: Remove one expected hash, then supply the correct hash and an incorrect hash. Unknown must remain distinct from verified and changed.

slides.title: 2 · Same-path replacements leave cached data stale
slides.fix: Bind caches to immutable release/content identity, or reject same-path modification.
slides.notes: A two-row invented sample file was loaded, then replaced with one row at the same path. load still returned two rows; clearing _load restored the correct one-row result. _load keys on table and resolved location, and check_data caches by location too. Choosing a different release path is a supported positive design; this finding concerns changed bytes at an unchanged path, not evidence that an immutable official release normally changes. Acceptance: Load two rows, replace with one at the same path, and confirm all counts and exports refresh or an immutable-release violation is explicit. Retain the different-path release control.

slides.title: 3 · Rebuild script does not enforce recorded inputs
slides.fix: Make the script consume the definition and verify resolved files and hashes before rebuilding.
slides.notes: Original definition records hashes. Same-source rebuild returned S1/S2; selecting another invented source returned S3 without mismatch warning. No malformed generated code executed.

slides.title: 4 · Empty cohort warning is absent from final problem summary
slides.fix: State empty cohort explicitly and preserve its reason at export.
slides.notes: Filtering the invented fixture to a nonexistent type returned zero rows and value_not_found/empty warnings, but unresolved_problems returned an empty list. The source then selects the success text No unresolved problems: one row per sample, and every joined record belongs to its own sample. The narrow join-grain claim is vacuously true, and an empty result may be legitimate. The concern is that the broad lead-in can hide the need to distinguish a genuinely empty population from a misspelled or unsupported filter. The live UI has not yet been observed for this case. Acceptance: Exercise a valid zero-result query, a misspelled value and an unavailable field. Each final summary should retain the different reason and limitation.

slides.title: 5 · Quoted request breaks generated Python
slides.fix: Serialize text and structured data with safe literal encoding or load a separate JSON file.
slides.notes: A normal request produced parseable Python. A request containing triple double quotes produced a SyntaxError when the generated script was parsed. The request is inserted into a triple-quoted module string without safe encoding; steps are also placed inside a raw triple-quoted JSON literal. Generated adversarial text was not executed. This demonstrates broken reproduction and a code-generation boundary, not an exploited deployment. Acceptance: Round-trip requests and values containing both quote styles, newlines, backslashes and triple quotes. Compare exact steps and cohort membership for benign generated scripts.

slides.title: What is verified so far
slides.fix: Read the test record before interpreting coverage.
slides.notes: Full suite: 170 passed, one skipped, zero failures. Earlier eight synthetic tests are included, not additional. No hosted/browser verification yet; targeted probes do not estimate general accuracy.
